planted:N01.title: Arithmetic of the sync basin for pulse-coupled oscillators
planted:N01.novelty_quote: The result adds a new member to the atlas of exotic basin geometries: alongside fractal, riddled, and tentacled basins, we now have a basin that is arithmetic.
planted:N01.behavior_summary: At linear charging, all-to-all pulse-coupled oscillators end fully synchronised with probability set by the prime factorisation of N (1-1/N^N for prime N; failures ~N^-(m-1) with m the least prime factor), and only equal-size cluster states survive.

planted:N02.title: Chemotaxis-induced linear instabilities and pattern formation in a reaction-diffusion model
planted:N02.novelty_quote: This has several novel features, which lead to some new physical phenomena.
planted:N02.behavior_summary: In a two-species reaction-diffusion (glycolysis-type) model with mutual chemotaxis, steady Turing pattern amplitude varies non-monotonically with chemotactic strength (re-entrant uniform/patterned transitions) and spots turn into stripes as chemotaxis grows.

planted:N03.title: Boundary- and Screening-Induced Bubbly Phases in Autophoretic Active Matter
planted:N03.novelty_quote: Despite these advances, controlled bubbly phases have, to the best of our knowledge, not been reported in particle-resolved systems with phoretic interactions.
planted:N03.behavior_summary: Autophoretic disks with chemo-attractive forces and chemo-repulsive torques above a no-flux wall form dense clusters filled with circulating cavities (boiling bubbles) or clusters that repeatedly rupture (bursting bubbles), between full collapse and dynamic clustering.

planted:N04.title: Topological instability and reentrant crystallization in active solids
planted:N04.novelty_quote: However, at a threshold value of non-reciprocity, we discover a qualitatively distinct mechanism for 2D melting, which we call topological instability.
planted:N04.behavior_summary: A 2D solid with transverse (odd) pair forces melts by defect-pair proliferation at any temperature above a threshold activity, and recrystallises at higher activity even at temperatures where the passive crystal is liquid.

planted:N05.title: Phase ordering kinetics in Light-Heavy-Vacancy model: unusual coarsening dynamics
planted:N05.novelty_quote: Unlike conventional phase-ordering systems, where coarsening proceeds through the formation and merger of ordered domains, here we find that domains formed at early times become unsustainable at later times.
planted:N05.behavior_summary: In a 1D two-species driven lattice gas on a fluctuating landscape, early ordered domains disintegrate and new ones form, giving two coarsening exponents (0.5 then 0.34) and a non-monotonic landscape length scale.

planted:N06.title: Fractional vortices in a spin-isotropic spiral spin liquid
planted:N06.novelty_quote: We uncover a rich family of vortex types involving concerted windings of spin directions, spiral-plane normals, and wave-vector orientations, yielding a $\mathds{Z}\times\mathds{Z}_{2}$ classification.
planted:N06.behavior_summary: In a classical Heisenberg spiral spin liquid on the square lattice, Monte Carlo shows a dense gas (~3%) of half-winding vortices of the spiral wave vector that bind into tight pairs and fuse below an order-by-disorder transition.

planted:N07.title: Odd diffusion and power-law correlations in chiral mass-transport processes
planted:N07.novelty_quote: However, the broken symmetries give rise to fundamentally new fluctuation properties.
planted:N07.behavior_summary: Isotropic mass-transfer rules with a fixed rotational sense (L-shaped chiral moves) produce r^-4 power-law density correlations in the steady state, with long-wavelength fluctuations minimised at an optimal chirality and a square-root cusp near maximal odd diffusion.

planted:N08.title: Phase Separation in a system of Brownian inertial rotors
planted:N08.novelty_quote: We uncover an emergent phase separation in a system of inertial dumbbells put into persistent rotation by a constant applied torque, breaking chiral symmetry, while interacting with each other through repulsive hard-core interactions.
planted:N08.behavior_summary: Purely repulsive inertial dumbbells driven by constant torques phase-separate into a dilute liquid and a dense hexatic phase (binodal, spinodal, t^1/3 coarsening), with rigidly rotating clusters; inertia is essential.

planted:N09.title: Merons Mediate Re-Ordering of Curved Rods Under Shear Flow
planted:N09.novelty_quote: These findings reveal a new mechanism to create and control merons and highlight the potential application of bent-core liquid crystals in designing functional material with specific optical and computational properties.
planted:N09.behavior_summary: Shearing the twist-bend nematic of bent rods along its helix axis makes it yield and nucleate charge-1/2 double-twist defect lines (merons) that rotate the helices into a stable orientation perpendicular to the flow.

planted:N10.title: Gliders on Aperiodic Monotilings: Cellular Automata on the Hat and Spectre
planted:N10.novelty_quote: Evolutionary search then discovers gliders on both monotilings; tracked by a sliding window that regenerates the patch along the flight, they travel one million rings at constant speed and heading.
planted:N10.behavior_summary: Simple threshold cellular automata on the aperiodic hat and spectre monotilings support gliders that travel indefinitely at constant speed with headings quantised to six directions.

planted:N11.title: Higher-Order Competition as a Minimal Mechanism for Spatial Pattern Diversity in Population Dynamics
planted:N11.novelty_quote: However, previous studies of the standard two-dimensional nonlocal FKPP equation reported only hexagonal arrays of population clusters.
planted:N11.behavior_summary: Adding a three-body competition term to a purely competitive spatial birth-death model breaks the hexagonal-spots-only restriction, giving stripes and gaps and an unusual spots-stripes-spots sequence.

planted:N12.title: Logarithmic Quasi-Long-Range Order and Novel Continuous Phase Transition in the Two-Dimensional $XY$ Model with $1/r^4$ Interaction
planted:N12.novelty_quote: First, using Gaussian spin-wave theory, we show that the low-temperature phase at $\sigma=2$ is a novel logarithmic quasi-long-range ordered (log-QLRO) phase, with $C(r)\sim(\ln r)^{-\eta_{\ell}}$ and $\eta_{\ell}=1/(2\pi\kappa)\propto T$ , where $\kappa$ is the dimensionless LR coupling strength.
planted:N12.behavior_summary: The 2D XY model with 1/r^4 couplings has a low-temperature phase whose correlations decay as a power of log r, entered through a continuous transition with power-law divergent correlation length (neither BKT nor Landau type).

planted:N13.title: Opinion dynamics under large-scale exogenous events
planted:N13.novelty_quote: For the case of the all-to-all noisy voter model under exogenous events, we unveil a rich phase diagram characterized by novel trimodal and asymmetric bimodal states.
planted:N13.behavior_summary: A noisy voter model hit by random population-wide opinion shocks shows trimodal and asymmetric bimodal stationary opinion distributions in addition to the usual unimodal and bimodal ones.

planted:N14.title: Networks of triblock ellipses: from kagome order to disordered porous networks
planted:N14.novelty_quote: This is – to the best of our knowledge – the first observation of a kagome lattice assembled from patchy ellipses.
planted:N14.behavior_summary: Hard ellipses with two polar sticky patches self-assemble into a kagome lattice that nucleates in one step directly from the gas (no chain intermediate), and into disordered porous networks at other conditions.

planted:N15.title: Emergence of Active Foams in a Minimal Cognitive Flocking Model
planted:N15.novelty_quote: We find that this regime exhibits a rich state diagram that combines characteristics of both limiting cases while giving rise to qualitatively new collective states.
planted:N15.behavior_summary: Self-propelled particles that only steer toward neighbours inside a narrow finite-range vision cone form a system-spanning, continuously restructuring fractal-like network of particle streams (dimension ~1.5) that never coarsens.

planted:N16.title: Self-Avoidance Governs Re-entrant Coil-Globule Transition of Inertial Active Brownian Ring Polymers
planted:N16.novelty_quote: Using Langevin dynamics simulations of an active Brownian ring polymer with translational and rotational inertia, we uncover an inertia-driven re-entrant coil–globule transition in the absence of any attractive interactions.
planted:N16.behavior_summary: A self-avoiding ring of active Brownian beads with rotational inertia collapses into a dense globule (over tenfold smaller) at intermediate activity with outward-polarised propulsion, then re-swells at high activity; translational inertia opposes collapse.

planted:N17.title: Coexistence phase of the two-dimensional Vicsek model
planted:N17.novelty_quote: Here we report on the diversity of band patterns observed in its coexistence phase –some of them never observed before–, but we also argue that most disappear in the infinite-size limit, leaving nevertheless a different picture than anticipated previously.
planted:N17.behavior_summary: In the coexistence phase of the 2D Vicsek model, side-by-side lanes of band trains travelling in opposite directions (and fat/inverse bands) form at particle level; long lanes buckle and the ordered band states are metastable.

planted:N18.title: Discrete time liquids
planted:N18.novelty_quote: Here we identify discrete time liquids – a new form of spatiotemporal order characterized by short-range temporal coherence as a result of time-solitons.
planted:N18.behavior_summary: A classical spin lattice driven only by a thermally fluctuating cavity mode shows robust period-doubled response that stochastically switches sign (temporal defects), giving finite temporal coherence.

planted:N19.title: Multi-scale patterns arising from competing chemotactic interactions
planted:N19.novelty_quote: We show that this can give rise to diverse patterns including long wavelength uninterrupted coarsening, Turing-like arrested coarsening, traveling waves as well as a novel class of mixed multi-scale oscillatory coarsening patterns, where a dense aggregate coexist with a dynamically spreading part of the population.
planted:N19.behavior_summary: A Keller-Segel model with chemotaxis toward a self-made attractant and a consumed nutrient produces a dense aggregate coexisting with travelling bands of cells.

planted:N20.title: Nonreciprocity Propels Nematic Defects
planted:N20.novelty_quote: Nonreciprocal interactions are a generic source of nonequilibrium dynamics, yet their consequences for nematic topological defects remain unexplored.
planted:N20.behavior_summary: Vision-cone-type nonreciprocal coupling on a nematic lattice makes +1/2 defects self-propel along their polar axis without active stress, and makes +1 defects split into three +1/2 and one -1/2 defect at strong nonreciprocity.
